headline: BUNKER HILL CONFIRMS New High-Grade Silver-Lead Veins: Up to 8.84 oz/t Ag, 23% Pb Near Existing Idaho Mine
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining (TSX: BNKR) confirmed two distinct high-grade galena-siderite veins within a 28.6-foot mineralized zone at its historic Idaho mine, grading up to 8.84 oz/t silver and 23.2% lead within 40 feet of existing development — open in all directions. The discovery extends 340 feet up-dip from the first intercept reported May 4, keeping the 25,000-foot campaign on track ahead of a planned June mine restart.

headline: LANDMARK RULING: Fortescue Ordered to Pay A$150M After Destroying 124 of 240 Indigenous Heritage Sites
snippet: Australia's Federal Court ordered Fortescue to pay A$150 million in cultural-loss compensation to the Yindjibarndi people after ruling the miner caused significant damage to heritage sites during development of its Solomon Hub iron ore operations in the Pilbara, with 124 of 240 sites completely destroyed. The decision — one of Australia's largest ever native title payouts — raises the stakes for A$1.8 billion in pending claims across the sector and flags permitting risk for miners on unresolved native title land.

headline: CAMECO HALTS Key Lake Mill, Cuts McArthur River Output — Flood Knocks Out Bridge to World's Largest Uranium Mine
snippet: Cameco halted its Key Lake uranium mill and reduced McArthur River production after the Smoothstone River Bridge collapsed in northern Saskatchewan flooding, severing the primary supply route to both operations. McArthur River's slurry tanks hold only 7–10 days of full production capacity with no timeline for resumption, and the company warned a prolonged disruption could affect its 2026 outlook for an operation that supplies roughly 12% of global uranium output.

headline: OMAI GOLD (TSX-V: OMG) Drills 23.8m at 3.86 g/t Au in Guyana Wenot — Superpit PEA Expected Q3
snippet: Omai Gold Mines (TSX-V: OMG) reported seven more drill holes at the Wenot deposit in Guyana, highlighted by 23.8 metres at 3.86 g/t gold and 16.9 metres at 3.49 g/t gold confirming multi-zone continuity across the deposit. An updated PEA incorporating a greatly expanded Wenot superpit design is due in Q3 2026, following April's 49.8% increase in Indicated resources to 1.45 million ounces.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD Hits 33.5 g/t Bonanza at Jubilee, Adds Second Rig to Expand Ontario District Play
snippet: Dryden Gold Corp. (OTC: DRYGF) returned a bonanza intercept from the Jubilee zone — 33.5 g/t gold over 0.5 metres within a 2.48 g/t over 12.65-metre composite — and is adding a second drill rig to accelerate resource definition at Gold Rock. Deeper down-plunge testing at Jubilee begins this summer as the company builds out what it describes as a fully funded multi-deposit Ontario district play.

headline: PERU VOTE COUNT DRAGS ON: Copper Mining Investors Fear Leftist Win Could Tax 12% of Global Output
snippet: Mining investors are growing uneasy as Peru's presidential vote count extends into mid-May ahead of a June 7 runoff between leftist Roberto Sánchez and conservative Keiko Fujimori, with business confidence at a two-year low and fears that a Sánchez win could hike taxes, shorten concessions, and pursue state-ownership rules over operations that represent roughly 12% of global copper output. Southern Copper alone has $10.3 billion in Peruvian investments at stake.

headline: US GOVERNMENT POURS $250M Into Sole American Antimony Producer — Pentagon Becomes Part-Owner of Montana Mine
snippet: The U.S. Department of Defense has invested over $44 million directly into U.S. Antimony Corp. (OTC: UAMY) and awarded the Thompson Falls, Montana smelter a sole-source $248 million supply contract, making the Pentagon a part-owner while the company expands production 500% to satisfy military demand for a mineral needed from bullets to nuclear components. China banned antimony exports to the U.S. in 2024, making UAMY the only domestic producer of a mineral the DoD classifies as critical to national security.

headline: LIBERTY GOLD Sells Goldstrike, Triggers Idaho Black Pine Federal EIS — Permitting Clock Starts at U.S. Forest Service
snippet: Liberty Gold (TSX: LGD) completed the sale of its Goldstrike project and reported that the U.S. Forest Service formally initiated the Environmental Impact Statement process for Black Pine — one of the most advanced undeveloped open-pit gold projects in the United States, in Idaho's Cassia County. The formal EIS kickoff means the permitting clock has started on a development that could deliver first gold if approved, with a public comment period now open.

headline: GOLD FALLS 16% FROM ITS PEAK But Institutional Forecasters Still See $5,000 — Here Is Their Case
snippet: With gold pulling back from its January 28 all-time high of $5,589 to around $4,678, analysts at JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, and the LBMA are maintaining their H2 2026 targets near $5,000, citing 755 tonnes of expected central bank buying, insufficient mine supply response at current cost curves, and the dollar's inability to sustain its rebound while the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked. The contrarian view: gold's 16% correction is within normal bull-market parameters, not a trend reversal.
